### This is a beta release

This build is for testing only. It is published as a pre-release, so it is not offered to
existing installations through the in-app updater — install it by hand from the assets below.

### Every host has to be paired again

This release fixes how a computer identifies itself, which renames every host once. Paired
hosts still hold the old name, so remove each host on both computers and pair them again with
the same pairing password. Custom host names and the shared host order have to be set once more.

### Fixes

- A shared display is no longer dropped, along with every paired host's input for it, when this
  computer cannot identify it for a moment. A display that is asleep, showing another host, or
  re-enumerated after a display-mode switch is kept and shown as unavailable until it identifies
  itself again. Only you remove a shared display.
- A computer no longer identifies itself by whichever network interface the system happened to
  enumerate first. On Macs every interface reports a private address and the winner changes, so
  one Mac introduced itself as three different hosts — which lost its pairings, its place in the
  host order and its custom name, and left two computers ordering their host cards in opposite
  directions. The identity is now fixed the first time it is worked out. Wake-on-LAN still uses
  the hardware address, which is what it is for.

### New

- Displays that report a different identifier per display mode can be merged. The MSI MPG 274U
  reports one identifier at 4K and another at 1080p, with no serial number in either, so nothing
  it reports can tell the two apart — only you can. Displays & Hosts now lists any display that
  belongs to no shared display and lets you merge it into one, and the claim syncs to every
  paired host. Switching still writes only to a display whose full identity matches exactly.

### Known limitations

- Merging only syncs between hosts running this version.
- The macOS DMG is ad-hoc signed but not notarized with an Apple Developer ID, so Gatekeeper may
  require manual approval.

### What to test

- Pair both computers again, then confirm their host cards run in the same order.
- Change your display's mode and confirm the shared display is not lost and needs no re-adding.
- Merge the display that appears after a mode switch, then switch modes both ways and confirm
  the display stays usable and its per-host inputs survive.
